Sampled HR@10 with one positive and 99 unique negatives measures success within 100 candidates; it is not full-catalog HR@10. Krichene and Rendle show that sampling can reverse model rankings even in expectation. Unique negatives avoid duplicates but do not remove this bias. Implication for this benchmark: full-catalog diagnostic improvements motivate hypotheses, but need not improve the fixed sampled selection metric. Preserve the evaluator and describe gains as sampled HR@10 gains. [Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)

With 200 users/category, one additional hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and the four-category macro average by 0.125 points—direct arithmetic for this setup. Compare models using paired per-user hit differences on identical candidates. A suitable uncertainty analysis resamples users within each category, keeping model pairs together, then recomputes the macro difference; exact McNemar tests can assess category-level binary differences. Uncertainty depends on discordant users, so aggregate scores alone are insufficient. These intervals condition on the fixed candidates and trained models; they do not capture candidate-sampling or training-seed variability. [Paired bootstrap](https://www.aclweb.org/anthology/W04-3250.pdf), [McNemar test](https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/generated/statsmodels.sandbox.stats.runs.mcnemar.html)

Fixed candidates improve comparability but remain vulnerable to adaptive validation overfitting: repeatedly selecting architectures, hyperparameters, or epochs can exploit peculiarities of those users and negatives. Model-selection research documents resulting optimism. Treat small winning gains and post-selection confidence intervals as exploratory; report trial counts and per-category changes, and reserve generalization claims for the host’s untouched final evaluation. [Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html), [Adaptive holdout reuse](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2015/hash/bad5f33780c42f2588878a9d07405083-Abstract.html)
